newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian protesters march, break police cordon.
newsitem.headline: Albanian protesters march, break police cordon.

text.p: Thousands of demonstrators broke through police cordons to occupy the main square in this southern city on Thursday in the second day of protests over the collapse of a pyramid investment scheme.

Around 10,000 people, chanting anti-government slogans, brushed aside riot police who briefly tried to prevent them entering the heart of the city. Some protesters hurled stones and vegetables at the security forces who did not fight back.

Police and demonstrators clashed violently in Vlore on Wednesday as security forces twice sought to disperse the crowds with water cannon and dogs. The protestors managed to re-group both times and the police finally let them pass.

"Vlore is ours, down with the government," the crowd chanted on Thursday as it pushed past the thin police lines. Many people sat down in the city's main Square of Independence, blocking access to the area.
The demonstrations were sparked by the failure earlier this week of the Gjallica pyramid scheme, which has its headquarters in Vlore and owes people an estimated $500 million.

The right-wing government, which many people blame for letting the pyramids flourish in post-communist Albania, started a partial compensation programme for investors from two failed funds this week but has said it cannot refund everyone.
